Interface Task<T extends @Nullable Object>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of the result
public sealed interface Task<T extends @Nullable Object>
Work that runs on a virtual thread, with its completion hooks.

The hooks, the progress and the messages are delivered through the UiExecutor: on the EDT with the UI module. Cancelling interrupts the thread; a task cancelled before its hooks run runs its onCancel(Runnable) hooks, then its onEnd(Runnable) hooks, and never its onSuccess(Consumer) or onFailure(Consumer) hooks, even when its work had already returned or thrown. A failure with no onFailure(Consumer) hook goes to the FailureHandler, as does a hook that throws; the remaining hooks still run. A task belongs to the scope it was started in: closing the scope cancels it.

Run a task with TaskService.run(Task, Scope), or return it from a command handler, which runs it. A handler that has nothing to run, such as one whose confirmation was declined, returns none().

Only core implements tasks: the interface is sealed, and its static methods and then(Function) make them.

    • of

      static <T extends @Nullable Object, P> Task<T> of(PublishingWork<T,P> work, Consumer<? super List<P>> onPublish)
      Returns a task of work that publishes partial results while it runs. onPublish receives the published values through the UiExecutor, in order, in batches: each call holds the values published since the previous one. Every value published before the work returns or throws reaches onPublish before the onSuccess(Consumer) or onFailure(Consumer) hooks run. Once the task is cancelled, the values not yet delivered are dropped, and onPublish isn't called again.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      P - the type of the published values
      Parameters:
      work - the work, given the task's context and the function that publishes a value
      onPublish - receives the published values, in batches
      Returns:
      the task
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if work or onPublish is null

    • none

      static <T extends @Nullable Object> Task<T> none()
      Returns the task with no work, which a command handler returns when it has nothing to run. Running it does nothing: no thread starts, no input is blocked, and its hooks never run. It may be run any number of times. It is one shared instance, which no chain owns: Task.none().then(next) returns it, without calling next.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      Returns:
      the task with no work

    • then

      <R extends @Nullable Object> Task<R> then(Function<? super T, ? extends Task<R>> next)
      Returns a chain that runs this task and, when it succeeds, calls next with its result through the UiExecutor, after this task's own onSuccess(Consumer) hooks, then runs the task next returns, in the same scope.

      The chain succeeds with the second task's result, or with null when next returns none(). It fails or is cancelled when either task fails or is cancelled; once this task has failed or been cancelled, next isn't called. Cancelling the chain cancels whichever task runs. next throwing fails the chain with that exception; next returning null fails it with a NullPointerException, and returning a task that has started or that belongs to a chain fails it with an IllegalStateException.

      This task's own hooks still run, for it alone; the chain's hooks run once, for the chain. A failure reaches the FailureHandler once, and only when neither the failing task nor the chain has an onFailure(Consumer) hook. This task belongs to the chain: running it on its own throws IllegalStateException.

      Type Parameters:
      R - the type of the chain's result
      Parameters:
      next - returns the task to run with this task's result
      Returns:
      the chain
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if next is null
      IllegalStateException - if this task has started, or already belongs to a chain
